issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide(), and the template's Main refers to Rideable. However, the solution repository introduces a different interface name 'Mountable' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java) which declares messageOnRide(), and the concrete classes Pig and Seal implement Mountable. Additionally, the solution contains an empty Rideable.java file. This name/type mismatch between 'Rideable' (spec/template) and 'Mountable' (solution) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and break code/tests that expect a Rideable interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Either (A) rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java and ensure it declares String messageOnRide(), and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable; remove or replace the empty Rideable.java file in the solution. Or (B) update the problem statement and template references to use Mountable instead of Rideable. Prefer option A to match the original specification (Rideable). Ensure the interface signature matches the specification (messageOnRide(): String).

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable' (the UML and example code use Rideable), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Mountable' and has classes (Pig, Seal) implement Mountable instead of Rideable. Additionally, Rideable.java in the solution is effectively empty. This inconsistent identifier use for the same conceptual interface (animals that can be ridden) creates confusion: students see 'Rideable' in the exercise and template but the reference solution uses 'Mountable', preventing a clear mapping between requirement and implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'Mountable' interface to 'Rideable' and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, and ensure Rideable.java contains the messageOnRide() declaration; or update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' consistently. Prefer renaming Mountable -> Rideable in the solution so it matches the UML and template examples.
